front: To what precision is a burette read?
back: To the nearest 0.05 cm³; record readings to two decimal places.
notes: Read the bottom of the meniscus at eye level.

front: What is each piece of titration apparatus rinsed with?
back: Burette: the solution it will hold. Pipette: the solution it will measure. Conical flask: distilled water only.
Red in acid, yellow in alkali, orange at the end-point.
Colourless in acid, blue in alkali.
Colourless in acid, pink in alkali.

front: What is the **end-point** of a titration?
back: The point at which the indicator just changes colour permanently.

front: Why is a white tile used?
back: To make the colour change at the end-point easier to see.

front: Why is universal indicator not used in titrations?
back: It changes colour gradually, so there is no sharp end-point.

front: Why must there be no air bubble in the burette jet?
back: If it is pushed out during the titration, its volume is counted as liquid, making the titre too large.

front: How is a pure soluble salt made by titration?
back: Titrate with indicator to find the volumes, repeat with the same volumes without indicator, then evaporate and crystallise.
